AgentInfo.description:
The agent running in a terminal tile, from herdr's agent status.
Absent when herdr knows of no agent there.

attention.description:
The agent became blocked or finished and needs a look. A finish
stays lit until the user reads it (`tile.seen`); blocked stays lit
until the agent's state changes. herdr's `done` status can outlive a
read, so this, not `status`, is the "unseen" flag.

name.description: The agent herdr detected or was told about, e.g. `claude`.

since_ms.description: When `status` last changed, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

unread.description:
The user marked the tile unread (`tile.mark_unread`) to come back to
it. Keeps `attention` lit whatever the agent does next, until the
user reads it (`tile.seen`). Saved with the session, so it survives a
relaunch.

AgentState.description: What the agent in a terminal tile is doing, per herdr.

oneOf.description: Waiting for the user, e.g. a permission prompt.
herdr doesn't know, or no agent runs in the pane.

agent.description: The agent herdr detected, e.g. `claude` or `codex`.

previous.description: The state before this change, when known.

AgentStatus.description: What herdr says the agent in a terminal tile is doing.

oneOf.description: Waiting for the user, e.g. a permission prompt.

ApplyMode.description: Where `layout.apply` puts a layout file's tabs.

oneOf.description: A new workspace named after the file, in the focused window.
Extra tabs in `workspace` (the focused one by default).

The file's tabs take the place of the workspace's active tab, which
closes. Its terminals detach; their herdr panes keep running.

Axis.description:
How a split lays out its two children: `horizontal` puts them side by side,
`vertical` stacks them.

oneOf.description: Liveness check; replies `pong`.
The whole object model; replies `session`.
Opens a window with one empty workspace.

Closes a window and its workspaces, herdr workspaces included (see
`workspace.close`).
Records a window's frame after the user moves or resizes it.

Opens a window's workspace sidebar, or collapses it to a rail or out
of sight, as `[sidebar] collapsed` says (restored on relaunch).
Every window; replies `windows`.
Workspaces of one window, or of all windows; replies `workspaces`.

Closes a workspace and its tabs, and its herdr workspace with every
tab and pane in it: their processes end. Closing a
window's last workspace closes the window.
Renames a workspace, and its herdr workspace too.

Sets the folder whose git branch the sidebar shows; without `path` the
core follows the focused terminal's working directory again.

Moves a workspace to another place in its window's list: the sidebar
order, which ⌘1…⌘8 and ⌘9 (the last) follow. Saved with the session.
It's Azulejo's own order: herdr's workspace order stays as it is.
Records the herdr workspace backing a workspace. Sent by the herdr adapter.
Tabs of one workspace, or of all workspaces; replies `tabs`.
Opens a tab with one tile (a terminal unless `content` says otherwise).
Closes a tab and its tiles; terminals detach, as with `tile.close`.
Lists tiles; replies `tiles`.
One tile; replies `tile`.

Closes a tile. A terminal's herdr pane is detached, not killed, unless
`kill` is set.

Focuses a tile. Focus alone doesn't count as reading its agent's
result: that's `tile.seen`.

The user has read the tile's agent's result: clears a finished
agent's attention (the done mark) and an unread mark
(`tile.mark_unread`) without moving focus. A blocked
agent keeps its attention until its state changes. The macOS shell
sends it once the tile has been focused, on screen, in the key window
for 0.75 s.

The user wants to come back to the tile: marks its agent unread, so
the tile shows the done mark (and counts as unread everywhere) until
`tile.seen`, whatever the agent does in between. Tiles without an
agent can't be marked (`invalid_state`).
Sets or clears a tile's title.

Lists one folder of a files panel (its root when `dir` is absent);
replies `files`. Doesn't watch it: see `files.expand`.

Lists a folder and watches it from now on: changes arrive as
`files.changed`. Shells send it when the user opens a folder.
Stops watching a folder and the folders open below it.

Opens the folders down to `path` and asks shells to select it
(`files.revealed`).

Shows or hides hidden and gitignored entries; toggles when `show` is
absent. Shells list their open folders again on `files.changed`.

Opens a path from a files panel beside the focused tile: a file in
the editor (a new terminal running it, to the right) or a folder in a
new terminal below; replies `created` with the tile.
Closes a files panel and stops watching its folders.

Moves or copies files and folders into a folder, on this machine or
between Local and a herdr machine (`scp`); replies `transferred`
when it's done, with what became of each.

Makes an empty file or folder, never replacing anything; replies
`file_created` with its path.

Deletes files and folders: to the Trash on Local, for good on a
herdr machine; replies `deleted` with what became of each.

A path on a herdr machine as an `ssh://` URL for apps with their
own SSH; replies `ssh_url`.
The focused tab's layout; emits `layout.changed` and replies `layout`.
Splits a tile and opens a new one beside it, which takes focus.
Moves focus to the neighbouring tile.
Swaps a tile with its neighbour in `direction`, or with tile `with`.
Moves a tile one step: into its neighbour's slot, or to the tab's edge.
Moves a tile's edge in `direction` by `amount` (negative shrinks).
Zooms a tile to fill its tab; leave `zoomed` out to toggle.

Opens a tile at the end of the tab's stack, whichever tile has focus; a
lone tile becomes master | stack. In a manual tab the stack is evened
out afterwards; in a dynamic tab the tile goes where `[layout] insert`
says.

Swaps a tile with its tab's master (manual tab) or moves it to the
front of the order (dynamic tab); focus stays on the tile.

Turns a Tile tab a quarter turn, as Bismuth's rotate: the master area
goes left → top → right → bottom (clockwise), or back with `reverse`.
`part` turns only the master area instead ("rotate part": masters
side by side or stacked), and `flip` toggles master left ↔ top
(`tall.py`'s rotate). A manual tab turns its whole split tree a
quarter turn, whatever its shape (`reverse` turns it back; `flip`
still toggles master left ↔ top). Monocle and Three Column have
nothing to turn: the command succeeds and changes nothing.
Gives every tile in the tab's stack the same size.
Switches a tab to a layout kind: `manual` or a dynamic one.

Switches a tab to `kind`, or back to its previous kind if `kind` is
already active.
Steps through the configured cycle of layout kinds.

Adds (or with a negative `delta` removes) masters in a Tile or Three
Column tab.

Grows (positive `delta`) or shrinks the master area of a Tile or Three
Column tab.
Moves a tile `step` places along its dynamic tab's order, wrapping.

Moves the divider of one split in a tab's tree, as dragging it does:
its `a` side gets `ratio` of the split, or leave `ratio` out to even
it out. A manual tab sets that split's ratio (what's nested keeps its
proportions). A Tile or Three Column tab turns it into its
parameters: the master ratio, Three Column's ratio (the centre stays
centred, so both side columns follow), or the sizes of the two tiles
either side of the divider. Monocle has no dividers.
Records the herdr pane a terminal tile views. Sent by the herdr adapter.

Gives an ended terminal tile a fresh herdr pane, keeping the tile's id
and place. The new pane gets its own herdr tab and the tile's cwd.

Reads a terminal's screen or history; replies `text`. History lives in
herdr, not in the tile.
Scrolls a terminal's view; replies `scroll`. 0 is the live bottom.

Finds lines containing `query` in a terminal's history; replies
`matches`. Runs over `recent_unwrapped` output in the core.

Streams events on this connection as `events.event` notifications;
replies `subscribed`. Answered by the API server, not the engine.
Ends a subscription made on this connection.

Opens a project layout file's tabs and tiles; replies `created` with
the workspace and first tab.
A tab or workspace as layout-file TOML; replies `layout_file`.

Every action the palette offers, with its current key chords;
replies `commands`.

Every keymap action with its context, default and current chords, and
whether the user's config set it; replies `keys`.

A commented `[keys]` template with every action and its default
chords, ready to paste into the config file; replies `text`.

Local plus herdr's saved machines and their connection state;
replies `machines`.

CommandEntry.description: One entry in the command palette.

action.description:
Keymap action name, when the entry is a keymap action. With `index`
for indexed actions (`switch_tab` + 3).

chords.description: Current bindings on this platform, in config syntax (`cmd+d`).

context.description:
The only context the action works in (`terminal`, `files`, `palette`,
`find`, `resize`…); `None` when it works anywhere.

id.description:
Stable id: the keymap action name (`split_right`, `switch_tab_3`), or
the method name for commands no key is bound to (`workspace.set_repo`).

method.description:
The protocol method it sends, if any; `None` for shell-only actions
(palette, sidebar, find…).

needs_tile.description: Acts on the focused tile, so the palette greys it out without one.

planned.description: Not supported yet; shown greyed out.

prompt.description:
Needs input before it can run (a URL, a path, a name): the palette
prompts for `prompt` first.

ConfigDiagnostic.description: A problem in the config file, for the shell's banner.

applied.description: False when the new file had errors: the previous config stays.

Created.description: IDs of what a command created; only the relevant fields are set.

DeleteItem.description: What became of one path of `files.delete`.

error.description: Why it couldn't be deleted; absent when it was.

trashed.description: Where it is in the Trash (Local only).

data.description:
For programs: what the error is about, such as `{"tile": "tile_…",
"direction": "right"}` or `{"param": "kind"}`. Over JSON-RPC these
fields sit in the error's `data` beside `code`.

`reason` narrows an `invalid_state` down for programs that act on
it: `no_neighbour` (no tile that way, for focus and swap) and
`no_edge` (no divider that way to move). Shells stay silent on both
when a key asked, since there's simply nothing there.

message.description: For people: shells show it as is, so it names no IDs.

oneOf.description: The request wasn't valid JSON.
Valid JSON, but not a request (e.g. no `method`).
A window, workspace, tab or tile doesn't exist.
The command doesn't apply right now (nothing focused, no neighbour that way…).
Not available in this build or configuration.
A service the command needs (herdr) isn't reachable right now.

Event.description: Something that changed in the core.

oneOf.description: Frame or sidebar changed.

sidebar_hidden.description: The sidebar is collapsed (a rail or hidden).

oneOf.description: Name, cwd or herdr binding changed.

A workspace's repository or branch changed, or it left a repository
(`git` absent): the sidebar shows the branch. Also visible as
`git` on `workspace.updated`.
A window's workspaces changed order.
A workspace's tabs changed order.
A tile's title or content changed (e.g. a terminal got its herdr pane).

A tile closed. `kill` asks the herdr adapter to kill the terminal's pane
rather than detach from it.

A terminal tile's agent started or stopped needing a look: it became
blocked or finished, went back to work, the user read its result
(`tile.seen`) or marked it unread (`tile.mark_unread`). Also
visible as `tile.agent.attention` on `tile.updated`.
A tab's tree, focused tile or zoom changed.
The focused window, workspace, tab or tile changed.

Folders a files panel has open changed on disk, or hidden entries were
toggled: list them again. Not saved.

`files.reveal` opened the folders down to an entry: shells expand them
and select it. Not saved.

Git status for a files panel's work tree, after it opens and after
changes. Not saved.

The core's link to Local's herdr came up or dropped; sent only when
that changes. `connected: true` comes once the core has re-checked
every bound tile's pane (a herdr restart gives each pane a new
terminal), so shells reattach waiting terminal tiles to current
panes. Not saved.

A herdr machine appeared, changed state or label. Not
saved.

A herdr machine left herdr's list (removed there, or hidden in
config). Its workspaces stay, unconnected. Not saved.

The agent in a terminal tile changed state, as herdr reports it.
Not saved.

The config file changed on disk and was read again (F25b). When it has
errors the previous config stays and `applied` is false. Not saved.

EventNotification.description: An event plus the subscription it's for: the event's own `event` and `data` fields, and `subscription`.

EventsSubscribe.description:
Parameters of `events.subscribe`. Every filter is optional; together they
narrow the stream (an event must pass all of them).

tile.description:
Only events about this tile: its own `tile.*` and
`agent.state_changed` events, layout changes of its tab, and focus
changes to or from it.

workspace.description:
Only events about this workspace: its own events, its tabs' and its
tiles', and `focus.changed` when focus lands in it. Events about no
particular workspace (`herdr.status`, window events) are left out.

FileEntry.description: One entry of a listed folder.

dir.description: A folder, or a symlink to one.

hidden.description: Starts with a dot. Only listed when hidden entries are shown.

ignored.description: Excluded by gitignore rules. Only listed when hidden entries are shown.

FileGitState.description:
A path's git state, for a badge. Folders take the strongest state of the
changes beneath them.

oneOf.description: An empty file.
An empty folder.

dirs.description: Folders whose entries changed: list them again. Absolute, resolved.

FilesCreate.description:
Makes an empty file or folder. Nothing is ever replaced: a name that's
taken (by a file, a folder or a link) fails with `invalid_params`, and
so does a folder that isn't there.

machine.description:
The machine to make it on (`machines.list` ID); Local when absent or
`local`. Leave it out with `tile`: a panel's entries are on its own
machine.

path.description:
The new entry: absolute, or relative to the panel's root. Its last
part is the name (not `.` or `..`).

tile.description:
A files panel (`files.panel`): `path` may be relative to its root,
and a remote panel's entry is made on its machine.

FilesDelete.description:
Deletes files and folders. On Local they go to the Trash (Finder's Put
Back works); on a herdr machine they're removed for good (`rm -rf` over
its SSH connection), so shells ask first. With `tile`, every path must
be inside that panel's root (not the root itself).

machine.description:
The machine the paths are on (`machines.list` ID); Local when absent
or `local`. Leave it out with `tile`: a panel's entries are on its
own machine.

paths.description: Absolute, or relative to the panel's root.

tile.description:
A files panel (`files.panel`): paths may be relative to its root,
and a remote panel's are on its machine.

FilesDir.description: A folder of a files panel.

dir.description: Absolute, or relative to the panel's root; the root when absent.

FilesGit.description:
Payload of `files.git`: the git state of every changed path in the
panel's work tree (and the folders above them). Replaces the previous one.

dir.description: The listed folder, absolute and resolved.

entries.description: Folders first, then natural name order (`a2` before `a10`).

error.description:
Why a remote folder couldn't be listed (the machine is unreachable,
the folder is gone). `entries` then holds the last listing, if any.

loading.description:
A remote folder the core hasn't listed yet: `entries` is empty and
`files.changed` names the folder when its listing is in.

machine.description: The herdr machine the files are on; absent for Local.

root.description: The panel's root, absolute and resolved (symlinks followed).

truncated.description: The folder had more entries than a listing returns; the rest are cut.

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the panel's root.

tile.description:
The files panel (`files.panel`) the path comes from: the path opens
beside the focused tile. Any tile works as the anchor instead when
`path` is absolute; the focused tile when absent.

oneOf.description:
A file opens in the editor: a new terminal tile to the right of the
anchor, in the file's folder, runs the editor on it (`vim <path>`).
It takes focus. A folder opens a terminal there instead, as
`terminal` does. `preview`, from builds that had preview tiles, means
this too.

A new terminal tile below the anchor, in the folder (a file's folder
for a file). It takes focus.

A folder opens in the editor: a new terminal tile to the right of
the anchor, in the folder, runs the editor on it (`vim <folder>`).
A file means its folder. It takes focus.

FilesPanel.description:
A files panel: a file tree outside the layout (the sidebar's Files view).
It answers `files.list`, `files.expand`, `files.collapse`,
`files.reveal`, `files.toggle_hidden` and `files.open` with its id as
`tile`, and its events carry that id.

With `machine`, the panel shows that herdr machine's files:
the core lists folders over the machine's SSH connection, off its
thread. A folder it hasn't listed yet comes back empty with `loading`,
and `files.changed` names the folder once its listing is in (or failed,
with `error`). Open folders are listed again every few seconds; nothing
is watched. `files.open` opens the editor and terminals on the focused
workspace's machine.

machine.description:
A herdr machine's ID (`machines.list`) whose files to show; Local
when absent or `local`.

panel.description: The panel to point at `root`; a new panel when absent.

root.description:
The folder to show; `~` expands to the home folder. On a remote
machine, an absolute path there.

path.description:
A file or folder under the panel's root: absolute, or relative to
the panel's root.

dirs.description: The folders to expand, root first.

path.description: The entry to select. Absolute, resolved.

FilesSshUrl.description:
A path on a herdr machine as an `ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path` URL, for
apps with their own SSH (the sidebar opens a remote file in Zed with it).
The host is the machine's SSH target as saved, an `~/.ssh/config` alias
staying an alias. Fails with `unavailable`, saying why, when another
app's SSH can't reach the machine as Azulejo does: `[herdr] ssh` is a
wrapper rather than OpenSSH, or the target isn't a plain host.

machine.description:
The machine the path is on (`machines.list` ID). Leave it out with
`tile`: a panel's entries are on its own machine.

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the panel's root.

tile.description:
A files panel (`files.panel`): `path` may be relative to its root,
and a remote panel's paths are on its machine.

show.description:
Show (true) or hide (false) hidden and ignored entries; toggles when
absent.

FilesTransfer.description:
Moves or copies files and folders into a folder. Nothing is ever
overwritten: a name already taken there gets a Finder-style number
(`notes 2.txt`, `notes 3.txt`, …).

Between machines it runs `scp` over the machine's shared SSH
connection: Local to a herdr machine (upload) or back (download). Both
ends on one remote machine, or on two, isn't supported.

folder.description: The folder they go into: absolute, on `to`.

from.description:
The machine the sources are on (`machines.list` ID); Local when
absent or `local`.

sources.description: Absolute paths of the files and folders, on `from`.

to.description: The machine the folder is on; Local when absent or `local`.

Focus.description: Where the user's focus is. Inner fields are `None` when that level is empty.

Frame.description: A window's frame on screen, in points, origin top left of the main display.

branch.description:
The checked-out branch, or the short commit when `detached`. Absent in
a repository with no commits yet only if git can't name the branch.

detached.description: HEAD points at a commit, not a branch.

dirty.description: Tracked files have changes (untracked files don't count).

HerdrRef.description:
The herdr pane a terminal tile views. Both IDs are kept: herdr changes a
pane's ID when it moves to another workspace, while the terminal ID is what
`herdr terminal attach` takes. The tab ID matters because closing a herdr
tab reports only the tab, and herdr keeps pane and tab IDs (but not the
process) across a server restart.

machine.description:
The herdr machine the pane runs on: `None` for Local, else herdr's
saved-machine ID. herdr IDs are only unique per server.

KeyBinding.description: One keymap action in one context, from `config.keys`.

context.description:
`global`, `prefix` (after the prefix key), or the context section it
sits in: `terminal`, `files`, `palette`, `find`
or `resize`.

current.description: The chords in effect now. Empty when unbound.

default.description:
The bundled defaults' chords, in config syntax (`ctrl+1..8` for
indexed actions). Empty when unbound by default.

default_text.description: `send_text` rows: the text the bundled defaults type on that chord.

source.description: `default` (bundled keymap) or `user` (the config file sets it).

text.description:
`send_text` rows (one per chord, terminal context): the text the
chord types now, as raw text. Absent when unbound, and on other rows.

base_dir.description:
What relative `cwd` and `path` values in the file resolve against.
Defaults to the file's directory, or the workspace's cwd for `toml`.

path.description: A layout file (`.azulejo.toml`). Give exactly one of `path` and `toml`.

workspace.description: For `new_tab` and `replace_tab`; the focused workspace by default.

step.description: Positions to move through the cycle; negative goes back. Defaults to 1.

path.description:
Also write the file here. Paths in it are made relative to its
directory where they're inside it.

tab.description: Export one tab. Without it, the whole workspace.

workspace.description: The workspace to export; the focused one by default.

LayoutKind.description: How a tab arranges its tiles.

oneOf.description: A split tree edited by hand; the tree is the source of truth.
Masters on one side, a stack on the other.
Every tile full size, the focused one on top.
Masters centred, stacks left and right.

delta.description: Change in the master area's share; negative shrinks. Defaults to 0.05.
How many masters to add; negative removes. Defaults to 1.

step.description: Places to move; negative moves towards the front. Defaults to 1.

LayoutParams.description: Every dynamic kind's parameters, remembered across switches.

amount.description: Share of the enclosing split to move the edge by. Defaults to 0.05.

flip.description:
Toggle master left ↔ top (and right ↔ bottom in a Tile tab) instead
of turning; a manual tree is rebuilt in tall shape. Not with `part`.

part.description:
Tile tabs: turn only the master area, so several masters sit side by
side instead of stacked.

reverse.description:
Turn anticlockwise: a Tile tab's master goes left → bottom → right →
top; a manual tab's tree turns back the other way.

path.description:
The split, as steps from the root of the tab's tree (`root` in
`session.get` and `layout.changed`): `a` for a split's first child,
`b` for its second. `""` (the default) is the root; `"ba"` is the
first child of the root's second child.

ratio.description:
The share of the split given to its `a` side, clamped to what the
layout allows (5–95 % per split; Tile's master area 20–80 %). Leave
it out to even the split out.

content.description: The new tile; defaults to a terminal.

direction.description: Which side of `tile` the new tile goes.

tile.description: The tile to split; defaults to the focused one.

content.description: The new tile; defaults to a terminal.

LayoutState.description:
A tab's layout, as `layout.changed` and `layout.get` report it.

Shells draw from `rects`: every tile's rectangle in the unit square, its
stacking order and whether it's shown (Monocle hides all but the focused
tile without resizing them). `tree` is the tab's split tree: the source of
truth for manual tabs, derived for dynamic ones.

order.description: Tile order of a dynamic tab, masters first; empty for manual tabs.

params.description: Every kind's parameters, as the tab remembers them.

direction.description: Swap with the neighbour this way. Give exactly one of `direction`, `with`.

with.description: Swap with this tile, which must be in the same tab.

MachineInfo.description: A herdr machine and how Azulejo's link to it is doing.

label.description: What the sidebar shows: "Local", or the label saved in herdr.

message.description: Why it's reconnecting or needs attention, when known.

oneOf.description: Not up yet since Azulejo started.
The link dropped; retrying with backoff.

Retrying won't help (password prompt, host key, no herdr there):
the user fixes it in herdr, e.g. `herdr machine reconnect <label>`.
Not connected on purpose: disabled in herdr or `connect = false`.

Node.description: One node of a layout tree.

ratio.description: Share of the space given to `a`, in (0, 1).

Notification.description:
A message the server sends without being asked, on a connection with a
subscription. On the wire it's a JSON-RPC notification: `method` plus
`params`.

oneOf.description: One event. `event` and `data` are exactly the event's own fields.

The subscriber fell behind and `dropped` events were skipped just
before the next one it receives.

OnExit.description:
What happens to a terminal tile when the process in its pane exits
(`exit`, ctrl+d, a finished command). Config `[terminal] on_exit`; a tile
can override it (layout files' `on_exit`).

oneOf.description: The tile closes, like any terminal window whose shell exits.
The tile stays, ended, offering Respawn or Close.

Orientation.description: Which side the Tile layout's masters sit on.

PaneMeta.description:
What herdr reports about a terminal tile's pane: enough to say what
runs there and where.

command.description:
The command running in the foreground when it isn't the shell, e.g.
`just dogfood`.

cwd.description: The pane's working directory (its foreground process's, when known).

title.description: The title the program in the pane set (OSC 0/2).

Placement.description:
Where one tile goes. `rect` is in the unit square, like
[`Node::rects`]; higher `z` draws on top; hidden tiles keep their rect but
aren't drawn (Monocle's tiles under the top one).

oneOf.description: The visible screen.
Recent output, soft-wrapped as on screen.
Recent output with soft wraps joined, for log-like text.

Rect.description: A rectangle in the unit square, origin top left.

oneOf.description: Done; nothing to return.
IDs of what the command created.
Where a terminal's view sits after `terminal.scroll`.
A folder of a files panel, from `files.list` or `files.expand`.
Lines that matched `terminal.search`.

scroll.description: With `locate`: the terminal's view when it was searched.

truncated.description: herdr cut the history short; older lines weren't searched.

oneOf.description: An event stream started; notifications carry this `subscription`.
A layout file, from `layout.export`.

path.description: Where it was written, if `path` was given.

oneOf.description: The command palette's entries, from `commands.list`.
The keymap, from `config.keys`.

prefix.description: The prefix key while prefix mode is on.

oneOf.description: herdr machines, Local first, from `machines.list`.
What `files.transfer` did, one item per source, in order.
What `files.create` made: absolute (resolved on Local).
What `files.delete` did, one item per path, in order.
`files.ssh_url`: the path as `ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path`.

line.description: 0-based line in the searched history, oldest first.

offset_from_bottom.description:
With `locate`: the `terminal.scroll` offset that puts this line in
the middle of the view.

row.description:
With `locate`: the line's first row in herdr's buffer, 0 being the
oldest row herdr keeps (a soft-wrapped line takes several rows).
Absent when the rows couldn't be matched up with the lines.

detached_herdr.description:
herdr panes whose tiles were closed here. Adoption skips them, so a
closed (detached) tile doesn't come back on the next relaunch. Pruned
once herdr no longer has the pane.

focused_window.description: `None` exactly when there are no windows.

oneOf.description: Machine groups, workspace rows and the footer.
Collapsed to a narrow rail: workspace numbers and agent states.
Collapsed out of sight.

Tab.description:
A tab: one layout tree. A tab always holds at least one tile; closing its
last tile closes the tab.

layout.description:
How the tiles are arranged. Old state files have none and
load as manual. For dynamic kinds `root` is derived from it.

recent.description:
Recently focused tiles, most recent first: directional focus breaks
ties with it.

tiles.description: The tiles in `root`, in no particular order.

zoomed.description: A zoomed tile fills the tab until unzoomed.

content.description: The tab's first tile; defaults to a terminal.

kind.description: The tab's layout kind, for a subtle hint in the tab bar.

TabLayout.description:
A tab's arrangement. For `manual` only `previous`, `params` and `kind`
matter; `order` and `weights` are empty.

manual.description:
The last hand-made tree, restored when switching back to manual while
it still holds the same tiles.

order.description: Tile order, authoritative for dynamic kinds: masters first.

previous.description: The kind before the last switch, for toggling back.

weights.description: Per-tile size weights within a column; absent means 1.0.

workspace.description: Only this workspace's tabs; all when absent.

index.description: New position within its workspace; past the end means last.

TabSummary.description: A tab and where it lives.

kind.description: The tab's layout kind, for a subtle hint in the tab bar.

offset_from_bottom.description: Lines above the live bottom; 0 returns to it.

lines.description:
How many lines of history to search; herdr's default when absent, or
all of it with `locate`.

locate.description:
Also work out where each match sits in herdr's buffer (`row`) and the
`terminal.scroll` offset that shows it mid-view, as a find bar needs.
Costs two more herdr calls.

keys.description: Key names in herdr's notation, e.g. `enter`, `ctrl+c`, `up`.

masters.description: How many tiles share the centre column: 1–10.

ratio.description:
The centre column's weight against each side column's `1 − ratio`,
as in Bismuth: 0.2–0.75. With three columns the centre takes
`ratio / (2 − ratio)` of the width (0.6 gives 3/7); with two (the
masters and one stack tile) it takes `ratio` itself.

command.description:
Command typed into the pane's shell once it starts. One element is
sent as a shell line (`npm run dev`); more are an argv, quoted for
the shell. herdr has no way to replace the shell, so the shell stays
when the command exits.

cwd.description: Working directory for a new pane.

env.description: Extra environment for a new pane, on top of `AZULEJO_*`.

herdr.description: Set once the herdr adapter has created or adopted a pane.

agent.description: Terminal tiles only: the agent herdr reports in the pane.

header.description: What the header strip shows; the core keeps it current.

pane.description: Terminal tiles only: title, cwd and command herdr reports for the pane.

kill.description: Kill the terminal's herdr pane instead of detaching from it.

TileContent.description: A tile's content and its kind-specific state.

shell says the same: e.g. `zsh` — `just dogfood`, `claude` —
`~/src/azulejo`, `README.md` — `~/code/shop`.

the shell. herdr has no way to replace the shell, so the shell stays

cwd.description: Working directory for a new pane.

env.description: Extra environment for a new pane, on top of `AZULEJO_*`.

agent.description: Terminal tiles only: the agent herdr reports in the pane.

focused.description: Whether this is the focused tile.

header.description: What the header strip shows; the core keeps it current.

pane.description: Terminal tiles only: title, cwd and command herdr reports for the pane.

workspace.description: Only tiles in this workspace; all tiles when absent.

masters.description: How many tiles sit in the master area: 0–10.

ratio.description: The master area's share of the tab: 0.2–0.8.

rotate_part.description:
Bismuth's "rotate part": masters split along the main axis instead of
across it, so with the master area on the left several masters sit
side by side rather than stacked (and the other way round on top).

TransferItem.description: What became of one source of `files.transfer`.

dest.description:
Where it is now, on the folder's machine; absent when it failed.
Moving something into the folder it's already in leaves it there
(`dest` is `source`).

error.description:
Why it failed. With `dest` set, the copy is in place but something
after it failed (a move's original couldn't be removed).

oneOf.description: The originals stay.

The originals go once their copy is in place (between machines: once
the upload or download succeeded).

Window.description:
An app window. It always holds at least one workspace; closing its last
workspace closes the window.

frame.description: Last known screen frame, in points; restored on relaunch.

sidebar.description:
How the sidebar shows: `full`, or collapsed as the `[sidebar]
collapsed` setting says (`rail` by default, or `hidden`).

sidebar_hidden.description:
The workspace sidebar is collapsed, to a rail or out of sight
(`sidebar` says which); restored on relaunch. The name predates the
rail.

workspace_name.description: Name of the window's first workspace.

visible.description:
`true` opens the full sidebar; `false` collapses it (`[sidebar]
collapsed`: a rail by default, or hidden).

WindowSummary.description: A window without its workspaces' contents.

Workspace.description: A workspace; maps one-to-one to a herdr workspace. It may have no tabs.

active_tab.description: `None` exactly when there are no tabs.

git.description:
The repository the workspace is in and its branch, as the core last
read it; absent outside a repository.

herdr_workspace.description: The herdr workspace backing this one, once the adapter has created it.

machine.description:
The herdr machine its terminals run on: `None` for Local, else
herdr's saved-machine ID.

repo.description:
The folder whose git branch the sidebar shows, when the user set one
(`workspace.set_repo`). Without it the core follows the focused
terminal's working directory.

machine.description:
The herdr machine its terminals run on: `"local"` (the default), or a
machine's ID or label from `machines.list`.

attention.description: Terminal tiles whose agent needs a look.

blocked.description: Terminal tiles whose agent is blocked, for the sidebar.

repo.description:
The folder whose branch it shows, when the user set one
(`workspace.set_repo`).

window.description: Only this window's workspaces; all when absent.

index.description:
New position within its window, from 0, counted once the workspace
has left its old place; past the end means last. A workspace stays in
its machine's group (the window's list is grouped by machine, as the
sidebar shows it), so a place past the group's edge stops there.

path.description:
A folder inside the repository; absent or empty follows the focused
terminal again.

WorkspaceSummary.description: A workspace and where it lives.

attention.description: Terminal tiles whose agent needs a look.

blocked.description: Terminal tiles whose agent is blocked, for the sidebar.

number.description:
Its place in the window's list, from 1: the sidebar order, and the
⌘ number that switches to it (⌘1…⌘8).

repo.description:
The folder whose branch it shows, when the user set one
(`workspace.set_repo`).
